title: Analista de Inteligência de Negócios Sênior

A nova marca surgiu pronta para o futuro, a partir da fusão entre a Aliansce Sonae e a brMalls, em 2023. Mas, essa trajetória começou bem antes. Tudo começou com a Aliansce, que inaugurou o primeiro shopping da região Nordeste e o segundo do Brasil em 1975. Em 2019, a fusão entre a Aliansce e a Sonae Sierra deu origem à Aliansce Sonae, tornando-se líder na administração de shoppings no Brasil, com 32 empreendimentos. Em 2006, surge a brMalls resultando em um portfólio de 30 ativos presentes nas cinco regiões do país. E assim, em 2023, a ALLOS surge com o encontro de duas potências nacionais do segmento, unindo forças para se tornar a mais inovadora plataforma de entretenimento, lifestyle, serviços e compras. A infraestrutura do Hospital conta com dez andares, nos quais estão distribuídos os serviços de emergência e de Unidade de Tratamento Intensivo (UTI) adulta, pediátrica e neonatal; maternidade; clínica médica, cirurgia-geral e bucomaxilofacial, neurocirurgia, psiquiatria, pediatria e ortopedia. Exames de imagem (raio X, tomografia, ultrassonografia, eletrocardiografia, ecocardiografia) e laboratoriais também são realizados na unidade. Devido à grande população de idosos da Zona Oeste, região assistida pelo Hospital Municipal Pedro II (HMPII), há duas Enfermarias destinadas ao atendimento desse público. O Centro de Tratamento de Queimados é outro diferencial entre os serviços oferecidos, e que dispõe de uma UTI exclusiva para prevenir infecções, que podem ser muito graves para quem está com queimaduras. Além disso, a unidade conta com a Coordenação de Emergência Regional (CER) Santa Cruz, que possui 39 leitos, e tem como objetivo absorver as demandas de menor complexidade, deixando o HMPII liberado para os casos de risco iminente de morte, necessidade de cirurgia urgente e/ou internação. Um diferencial deste CER é o fato de possuir atendimento especializado em Psiquiatria e Obstetrícia. Responsabilidades e atribuições Realizar atendimento a exames admissionais, demissionais, periódicos, avaliação médica, retorno ao trabalho, mudança de função, encaminhamento ao INSS ou a médicos especialistas. Orientar restrições e recomendações conforme necessidade de cada caso. Realizar avaliações de atestados médicos, acidentes de trabalho e outras conforme a necessidade da Instituição. Requisitos e qualificações Ensino Superior Completo em Medicina. Residência Médica ou Título de Especialista em Medicina do Trabalho. Registro Ativo no Conselho da Classe. Experiência mínima de 06 (seis) meses comprovada como Médico do Trabalho. Informações adicionais Local de trabalho: Santa Cruz - RJ; Escala de trabalho: 20 horas semanais; Horário: A combinar. #J-18808-Ljbffr

title: Dressing & Signage Cluster Manager
description: Overview FIFA has established a Local FIFA Subsidiary in Brazil to work together with FIFA Zurich to deliver the biggest women’s sporting event in the world, the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027™ (“FWWC2027”) that for the first time ever is hosted in South America in Brazil. Now is your time to be part of the workforce that is creating this unique and unforgettable experience. Department Technical & Infrastructure Location Brazil Position Summary The Dressing & Signage Cluster Manager reports to the Dressing and Signage Senior Manager, serving as a key member of the FIFA27 Operations team in close collaboration with the Venue Management team and other stakeholders. The FIFA Women's World Cup Brazil 2027™ requires an outstanding look and feel project to be delivered in a seamless tournament experience. The Dressing & Signage Cluster Manager is responsible for leading the venue branding, look and signage operations and delivery strategy from planning through implementation to closure across all FIFA Official Sites. This position is responsible for overseeing the delivery of a world‑class dressing and signage project for all target groups attending matches of the FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027™, ensuring that the look and feel is up to FIFA quality standards. The role assumes event operational proficiency, venue dressing, signage and wayfinding knowledge with project management skills to directly oversee the dressing implementation at four FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027™ stadia. They will ensure that key project deliverables and deadlines are met within their sites and will be required to input into strategic project decisions taken by senior members of the team. They will oversee contracted provider operations within their sites, ensuring that all are managed successfully and efficiently while monitoring budgetary spending within agreed limits. They will ensure that precedents and strategic directives from the Head of Dressing and Signage and Senior Dressing and Signage Manager are followed as required by the members of the team. The role will collaborate closely with other dressing, signage, wayfinding, and non‑competition managers to maximize creativity and ensure consistency across all stadiums. Key Responsibilities Oversee the turnkey planning of dressing and signage implementation across all official sites during the planning phase, and stadium dressing for 3-5 stadia closer to the tournament. Collaborate with the other Stadium Dressing Managers and ensure that precedents are followed to guarantee consistency across all tournament stadiums. Work closely with the Non‑Competition Dressing Managers and the Wayfinding and Signage Managers as well as other Functional Area Managers, to maximize efficiencies across the wider project. Serve as the focal point for all general stadium dressing questions or requests from the Head of Department. Oversee contracted provider planning, production and implementation for all stadiums within the assigned sites. Constantly monitor the budgetary impact of dressing operations and report updates to the Senior Manager and Head of Department regularly. Provide strategic input into the stadium dressing planning process and offer expertise when required. Adhere to project deadlines and deliverables as instructed by senior members of the department. Maintain daily liaison with other members of the wider Dressing and Signage team to ensure efficient planning and delivery is optimized at all stages of the project. Liaise with stadium owners and operators as required to gain approval on implementation plans. Present to senior team members, management and other FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027™ functional areas as and when required. Attend department‑specific and organization site visits at assigned stadiums and other stadiums or official sites. Input into the site‑specific dressing strategies utilizing expertise from previous events and directives from management. Act as the main stadium dressing point of contact for Dressing and Signage Venue Managers and other Functional Area Venue Managers within the assigned sites during the implementation phase of the project. Participate in the creative design process for stadiums within the assigned sites. Assist with the recruitment of Dressing and Signage project team members in collaboration with the senior department leads if required. Ensure the needs of internal FIFA functional areas are captured and delivered against within the assigned sites. Contribute to project management and knowledge management initiatives including event debriefs, and knowledge capture and documentation activities. Possibly relocate to a Host City for up to three months to act as a Dressing and Signage Venue Manager at an allocated stadium during the event periods. Your Profile Minimum 4+ years of experience delivering dressing, signage, branding or look projects for events of a similar scale to FIFA World Cups, Olympic Games, etc., or a minimum 2 years’ experience managing major sports events in a role that included the delivery of comprehensive dressing or signage related activities. A working understanding of the technical aspects of delivering dressing and signage projects (i.e. production methods, installation techniques, materials etc.). Strong understanding of stadium look and feel requirements and large‑scale temporary installations. Budget management experience on complex and multi‑faceted events and projects. Experience managing providers of services for world‑class events. Knowledge of event planning, requirements and event project management processes for large sporting events. Significant stakeholder management experience across multiple organizations and departments. Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with the ability to assess and implement effective solutions. Bachelor’s or master’s degree in an appropriate subject (or adequate training/vocational education) in Design, Architecture, Project Management, or a related field. Proficiency in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Visio & Project) and planning software and online collaboration tools. Readiness to learn new technology processes, systems and programs, as the role will require extensive use of the appointed Dressing and Signage Supplier(s) project, content and scoping management systems. Will attend site visits and be away from home for periods of time, including on‑site attendance during the tournament period. Right to work in Brazil. Fluent in English (spoken and written). Fluent in Portuguese (spoken and written). Ability to relocate to Rio de Janeiro. #J-18808-Ljbffr

title: A CARREIRA DO FARMACÊUTICO DE ASSUNTOS REGULATÓRIOS
description: A carreira farmacêutica especializada em regulação sanitária de indústrias, distribuidoras e empresas do varejo farmacêutico é uma das mais valorizadas pelo mercado de trabalho. Esta carreira possui grande projeção profissional no meio industrial e em órgãos reguladores, em que existe maior complexidade nas atividades realizadas pelo profissional, consequentemente as maiores remunerações estão em localidades que possuem polos industriais farmacêuticos, como São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, Rio Grande do Sul, Paraná, Brasília e Pernambuco. Ser especialista em regulação sanitária exige do profissional aptidão para tarefas administrativas, conhecimentos aprofundados em legislação sanitária nacional e internacional e capacidade de negociação, liderança, comunicação e gestão. O inglês é indispensável e o espanhol pode ser um diferencial para grandes empresas farmacêuticas brasileiras, que detêm filiais na América Latina. A competição profissional nesta carreira é acirrada, pois a atuação não é restrita ao farmacêutico por força de lei. Dessa forma, o profissional formado em Farmácia compete com praticamente todos os profissionais de saúde, advogados e até administradores de empresas. Responsabilidades na indústria de medicamentos e em consultorias especializadas: Acompanha os processos de pesquisa e desenvolvimento de novos produtos; Analisa relatórios de qualificação e validação; Acompanha e avalia o mercado e os lançamentos de novos produtos dos concorrentes; Administra e executa o processo de registro de novos produtos farmacêuticos na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa); Acompanha diariamente as publicações da Anvisa no Diário Oficial da União (D.O.U.); Discute novas resoluções em Consultas Públicas na Anvisa; Acompanha e implementa novas resoluções e regras sanitárias; Recebe e acompanha auditoria sanitária; Administra o processo de revalidação do registro de produtos; Acompanha o sistema de atendimento ao cliente (SAC) e registros do setor de farmacovigilância; Orienta o departamento de marketing em publicidades e propagandas; Orienta o departamento jurídico em demandas de cunho sanitário; Verifica os registros e cadastros sanitários do estabelecimento. Responsabilidades nos órgãos reguladores: Acompanha o cumprimento de normas e legislação por parte das empresas; Propõe e debate com o mercado o desenvolvimento de novas resoluções e regulamentações; Fiscaliza a qualidade e o seguimento de regras na produção de produtos farmacêuticos; Fiscaliza a comercialização de produtos farmacêuticos; Regulamenta o preço dos medicamentos; Regulamenta os tipos de medicamentos e suas formas de comercialização; Regulamenta o comércio farmacêutico e suas características de consumo. Orienta e acompanha o departamento jurídico em demandas de cunho sanitário; Cuida dos registros e cadastros sanitários do estabelecimento; Orienta e fiscaliza condições de estoque e armazenamento de produtos; Acompanha e fiscaliza condições de transporte e distribuição de produtos farmacêuticos. Áreas de atuação: Indústrias farmacêuticas; Empresas de logística farmacêutica; Consultorias especializadas; Vigilância sanitária de estados e municípios (Visa). O curso de graduação em Farmácia é o mais indicado para profissionais que desejam seguir carreira em Assuntos Regulatórios principalmente na indústria de medicamentos. É importante ressaltar que profissionais que desejam atuar em agências reguladoras, como a Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa), é necessária a aprovação em concurso público específico. O curso de graduação em Direito também têm peso e relevância. Uma especialização em Assuntos Regulatórios é obrigatória. Existe também a opção de especialização em Logística Farmacêutica para os profissionais que atuam especificamente em distribuidoras. Para que o profissional se mantenha atualizado é imprescindível que ele acesse, com periodicidade, o conteúdo específico da área farmacêutica publicado no Diário Oficial da União e o site da Anvisa, para manter-se informado sobre novas legislações e consultas públicas vigentes. O ICTQ - Instituto de Pesquisa e Pós-Graduação para o Mercado Farmacêutico tem em seu portal na internet um canal de notícias atualizado diariamente com as novidades demandadas pela Anvisa, vale a pena acompanhá-lo. O mesmo Instituto é pioneiro no Brasil com curso de especialização em Assuntos Regulatórios na Indústria Farmacêutica, além de oferecer a pós graduação em Gestão, Logística e Distribuição Farmacêutica. #J-18808-Ljbffr

Ensure subsea systems are operated within approved operational and insurance limitations. Manage subsea systems during maintenance, refurbishment, or standby periods. Coordinate subsea team activities including work allocation and watchkeeping in supervisory scenarios. Support planning and execution of maintenance, repair, and overhaul of subsea equipment to ensure operational readiness at all times. Escalate system downtime or reduced functionality to vessel leadership and onshore management where required. Assist with reporting, documentation, and technical returns for subsea systems. Maintain awareness of operational factors including vessel manoeuvrability, weather conditions, currents, and seabed characteristics. Support training and development of junior technicians and subsea personnel. O Centro de Tratamento de Queimados é outro diferencial entre os serviços oferecidos, e que dispõe de uma UTI exclusiva para prevenir infecções, que podem ser muito graves para quem está com queimaduras. title: Jr Project Manager
description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission‑critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI‑powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well‑being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Kyndryl Project Managers oversee the delivery of major projects within scope, schedule, and budget. You’ll be the driving force for every aspect of a program’s success, and the “conductor” who orchestrates everyone’s efforts to make beautiful music together. As the single point of contact to the client, you’ll also be the living embodiment of Kyndryl’s reputation every day. As Project Manager, you have command of a very full and detail‑oriented calendar. You’ll be constructing detailed project plans, managing teams, and leading meetings, status calls, and planning and cadence meetings. You will analyze and mitigate risks, manage finances, make sure the team has the right skills, then plan and delegate activity to hit deadlines, deliver on SLAs, and generally delight our clients. Of course, plans often evolve as a project unfolds, so you’ll need to practice continuous structural thinking and take ownership for value delivery, not just task scheduling. But as important as planning and organization are, communication is 90% of the job. You’re the single point of contact with the client, partners, and all stakeholders, supporting them and ensuring they get what they need. You’re also the bridge to every other team on the project, including both technical and account roles. The result is an exciting multicultural, often multilingual environment. Bottom line: You need to like interactions with other people and know how to be kind and empathetic but also assertive — and handle customer change requests with diplomacy. You’re going to be meeting a lot of people, networking, and forging relationships. Our “one team with the customer” concept means you’ll develop especially strong partnerships with the client and elsewhere. Some projects or clients even involve “embedding” with the client at their location. This puts more visibility on you personally, but it also gives you more opportunity to add value to the relationship. It’s a great way to hone your service and people skills, and it lays the groundwork for career growth both laterally and vertically. Your Future at Kyndryl Becoming a Project Manager at Kyndryl is an excellent gateway to many different paths. You’ll be creating a well‑rounded skillset while gaining professional certifications and qualifications. You can evolve horizontally into other technical or non‑technical areas such as Technical Service Architect, or you can move vertically to become a senior project manager or program manager. There are many different types and flavors of PM roles, so everyone can find the opportunity that suits them best. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer‑focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical And Professional Experience SCRUM or Project Management skills Organization and planning skills Bachelor's degree in IT, Networking, or Business Administration MBA or postgraduate degree in project management Availability for travel Preferred Technical And Professional Experience Advanced English MS Project or other Project Management software Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to interact confidently with stakeholders of all levels Being You The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. What You Can Expect Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid‑friendly culture that supports your well‑being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in‑demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting‑edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands‑on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. People management experience — hiring, coaching, and developing teams. Experience with external partners, affiliates, marketplaces, loyalty programs, or B2B/B2B2C channels. MBA or advanced degree (equivalent hands‑on experience equally valued). Why join Agoda Work on high‑impact, global business problems with direct visibility to senior leadership. title: Senior Manager, Ocean Policy
description: Conservation International protects nature for the benefit of humanity. Through science, policy, fieldwork, and finance, we spotlight and secure the most important places in nature for the climate, biodiversity, and for people. With offices in 30 countries and projects in more than 100 countries, Conservation International partners with governments, companies, civil society, Indigenous peoples, and local communities to help people and nature thrive together. Position Summary This position is open for consideration in the following locations in the Americas, with preference for candidates based in time zones that can accommodate calls with colleagues in Europe and Africa: Arlington-US, Brazil(remote), Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guyana, Mexico, Suriname, Peru Over the last 10 years, CI has developed a comprehensive Blue Climate program spanning over 20 countries dedicated to identifying and addressing science and policy priorities for oceans and climate globally. The Blue Climate program within the Center for Oceans at CI works closely with our field programs across the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa to design and implement innovative approaches to (1) implement nature‑based climate adaptation solutions that improve coastal and marine communities’ livelihoods and resilience while also conserving ecosystems and biodiversity; and (2) conserve and restore coastal blue carbon ecosystems (mangroves, salt marshes, and seagrass meadows) for climate change mitigation. The Blue Climate program also has key leadership roles in advancing climate mitigation and adaptation priorities into national and regional coastal management and science through the International Blue Carbon Institute, Blue Carbon Initiative, the International Partnership for Blue Carbon, the Global Mangrove Alliance and the Global Green‑Gray Community of Practice, and policy with the Center for Policy and Incentives. Under the supervision of the Director, Ocean Policy, the Senior Manager, Ocean Policy, is a self‑motivated, creative team member integral to the long‑term growth and success of CI’s Blue Climate program and Ocean Policy team. The Senior Manager, Ocean Policy will support the development, implementation and management of strategic international policy‑based approaches and programs to achieve CI’s Ocean Policy goals spanning coastal resilience, climate mitigation, green‑gray infrastructure, blue‑carbon ecosystems and ocean‑climate integration. Together with the Director, Ocean Policy, they will work with CI’s Center for Policy and Incentives to ensure alignment with CI’s larger international and national policy programs and priorities, including providing technical inputs and guidance on ocean‑climate issues. The position will also work closely with teams across CI including other programs within the Center for Oceans and the Moore Center for Science and Solutions to ensure alignment and integration of ocean policy priorities with all related CI programs and topic areas, including biodiversity, finance, and community fisheries. Responsibilities International Ocean Policy Manage strategic policy initiatives to achieve CI’s Ocean Policy goals spanning coastal resilience, green‑gray infrastructure, blue carbon, and other ocean‑climate areas which integrate and align international and national policy goals. Work closely with CI’s Center for Policy and Incentives to ensure ocean‑climate strategies and approaches are aligned with international and national policy programs and priorities. Play a key role in project development, fundraising, implementation, communications, and broader capacity building for the Ocean Policy program. Contribute to the drafting and revision of CI ocean policy positions, policy briefs, guidance documents, and other technical resources. Play a key role in representing the Center for Oceans within the CI delegation to international policy meetings related to climate, biodiversity, and oceans, such as the UNFCCC climate COP and intersessional meetings. Additionally, support CI’s strategic engagement in these spaces (e.g., side events, meetings with countries and partners). Support the development and management of relationships and partnerships with government representatives and like‑minded organizations to accelerate and achieve CI ocean policy objectives in close coordination with CI’s international policy team and relevant country programs. Ocean Policy Advancement in Priority Countries In partnership with CI country programs, the International Blue Carbon Institute, and the Center for Policy and Incentives, support the development and implementation of national or regional ocean policy objectives and programs which are aligned with and inform CI’s Blue Climate and broader policy priorities. Provide CI programs and partners with strategic support, technical expertise, and/or capacity building for the integration of coastal ecosystems into Nationally Determined Contributions and implementation plans, national climate and ocean policy, greenhouse gas inventories, NBSAPs and other related components of ocean‑climate policy. As needed, facilitate in‑person and virtual meetings, workshops, and related events with national governments and local partners to advance the priorities of CI country programs in alignment with national objectives. Support the Ocean Policy Director in scoping new policy activities in accordance with existing CI programs. Blue Climate Program Contribute to strategy development, planning processes, fundraising, team initiatives/special projects, reporting and communication efforts as needed. Coordinate with other teams across the Blue Climate network team to ensure programmatic alignment and synergies between CI projects. Other duties as assigned by supervisor. Working Conditions Frequent international travel (25% or more) is required. Ability to work in remote locations or under difficult working conditions. This position follows a hybrid work structure, working some days from the office and some days remotely. Guidance will be shared during the interview process. Requires working remotely with colleagues in other locations and time zones. Flexible working hours: Frequent early morning and evening meetings, and occasional work over weekends, to accommodate colleagues in other time zones or high‑level policy events. This position follows a hybrid work structure, working some days from the office and some remotely. Guidance will be shared during the interview process. Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree 5 to 7 years of experience working in international climate and/or ocean policy mechanisms and fora. Understanding of government processes and the overall policy engagement environment. Strong organization, project management, and prioritization skills. Excellent time management skills and ability to adapt in a fast‑paced, changing environment. Ability to work both independently and as part of a diverse, international team. Experience partnering with, and influencing, key stakeholders and building strong partnerships across public and private sectors and civil society. Excellent written and oral communication skills, and ability to effectively communicate complex information to a diverse audience. Enthusiasm and capacity for learning scientific and related basis for specific conservation outcomes as needed to support policy priorities and processes. Fluency in written and spoken English. Preferred Bi‑lingual or multilingual in official UN languages. Expertise in coastal blue carbon and marine ecosystems, climate change science, and/or nature‑based solutions Master’s degree or other advanced degree in environmental policy or related field. Experience working globally in a range of cultural settings. To apply for this position, please submit a resume and cover letter. This position will remain open until filled. Good working knowledge of workforce planning systems, tools, and practices. Experience supporting or coordinating operational venue teams at large-scale events. Understanding of data-driven decision-making and workforce planning processes in complex environments. Demonstrated ability to manage projects, prioritise tasks effectively, and work with a level of independence. Experience supervising team members and contributing to team performance through positive leadership and collaboration. Strong communication skills, both written and verbal. Demonstrated adaptability, with experience supporting discussions, problem-solving, and stakeholder coordination. Experience working in a multicultural and/or multinational environment. Fluent in English, both written and spoken. Fluent or advanced Portuguese. Technology Skills Proficient in Microsoft Office tools (Word, PowerPoint, Visio & advanced Excel). title: Analista de Frotas- Combustível
description: Responsabilidades Planejar, controlar e analisar as atividades relacionadas ao abastecimento da frota, assegurando a correta gestão do consumo de combustível, a confiabilidade das informações, a otimização dos custos operacionais e a conformidade dos processos. Atuar na geração de indicadores, auditoria de abastecimentos, gestão de fornecedores e suporte técnico à tomada de decisão, contribuindo para o aumento da eficiência operacional e sustentabilidade da frota. Principais atividades Monitorar e validar diariamente os abastecimentos realizados pela frota, verificando volumes abastecidos, tipo de combustível, veículos, motoristas e postos utilizados. Gerenciar os saldos de abastecimento por veículo, motorista e período, identificando desvios e oportunidades de melhoria. Controlar e realizar a conciliação dos abastecimentos junto às operadoras de cartão combustível, postos, bandeiras e demais fornecedores. Acompanhar a utilização de cartões de combustível, analisando faturas e identificando inconsistências ou irregularidades. Realizar liberações e bloqueios de abastecimento conforme políticas e regras de negócio estabelecidas pela empresa. Calcular, monitorar e analisar os principais indicadores de desempenho relacionados ao consumo de combustível, incluindo consumo médio (km/l), custo por quilômetro rodado, desvio de consumo e variação de preços por fornecedor. Elaborar relatórios gerenciais diários, semanais e mensais sobre consumo, custos, desempenho operacional e tendências de abastecimento. Desenvolver análises comparativas entre veículos, motoristas, rotas e unidades operacionais, identificando oportunidades de melhoria. Identificar padrões de consumo atípicos, divergências entre quilometragem e abastecimento, bem como possíveis desperdícios. Elaborar projeções de consumo e despesas com combustível para apoio ao planejamento orçamentário. Acompanhar a evolução dos preços dos combustíveis por região e fornecedor, subsidiando negociações comerciais e estratégias de abastecimento. Propor ações para redução de custos e aumento da eficiência operacional por meio da análise de dados e indicadores. Participar da elaboração, acompanhamento e controle do orçamento de combustível da frota. Auditar divergências entre abastecimentos realizados e parâmetros operacionais esperados, verificando possíveis inconsistências ou desvios. Acompanhar a regularidade fiscal dos abastecimentos, conferindo documentos fiscais e apoiando processos relacionados à legislação tributária aplicável. Identificar indícios de fraudes, irregularidades ou não conformidades nos processos de abastecimento, reportando-os à gestão para as providências cabíveis. Atuar como referência técnica para esclarecimento de dúvidas relacionadas às políticas de abastecimento, utilização de cartões, postos credenciados e limites operacionais. Apoiar a implantação, parametrização e melhoria de sistemas de gestão de combustível, telemetria e monitoramento da frota. Ministrar orientações e treinamentos para motoristas e equipes operacionais quanto aos procedimentos e políticas de abastecimento. Participar de projetos voltados à eficiência energética, redução de custos operacionais e sustentabilidade da frota. Experiência em gestão de frotas, logística, transportes ou áreas correlatas. Vivência em controle e gestão de abastecimento de frotas. Experiência na elaboração de indicadores gerenciais, análise de dados e controle de custos. Atuação com processos de conciliação de abastecimento, auditoria e relacionamento com fornecedores. Conhecimento dos principais indicadores de desempenho de combustível, como consumo médio (km/l), custo por quilômetro rodado, desvios de abastecimento e eficiência operacional. Conhecimento em processos de auditoria e conciliação de abastecimentos. Diferenciais Conhecimento em Power BI ou outras ferramentas de Business Intelligence. description: Preparar o carro de distribuição das refeições servidas para os pacientes, incluindo desjejum, almoço, merenda jantar e ceia. Desde dezembro de 2015, a SPDM/PAIS é responsável, em parceria com a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde do Rio de Janeiro, pelo gerenciamento do Hospital Municipal Pedro II . A infraestrutura do Hospital conta com dez andares, nos quais estão distribuídos os serviços de emergência e de Unidade de Tratamento Intensivo (UTI) adulta, pediátrica e neonatal; maternidade; clínica médica, cirurgia-geral e bucomaxilofacial, neurocirurgia, psiquiatria, pediatria e ortopedia. Devido à grande população de idosos da Zona Oeste, região assistida pelo Hospital Municipal Pedro II (HMPII), há duas Enfermarias destinadas ao atendimento desse público. O Centro de Tratamento de Queimados é outro diferencial entre os serviços oferecidos, e que dispõe de uma UTI exclusiva para prevenir infecções, que podem ser muito graves para quem está com queimaduras. Além disso, a unidade conta com a Coordenação de Emergência Regional (CER) Santa Cruz, que possui 39 leitos, e tem como objetivo absorver as demandas de menor complexidade, deixando o HMPII liberado para os casos de risco iminente de morte, necessidade de cirurgia urgente e/ou internação. Um diferencial deste CER é o fato de possuir atendimento especializado em Psiquiatria e Obstetrícia. Aqui, você fará parte de um time comprometido com a qualidade do cuidado e a experiência do paciente, atuando de forma colaborativa e com foco contínuo em excelência. Responsabilidades e atribuições Coletar materiais biológicos utilizando instrumentos e métodos apropriados para a realização dos exames, bem como possibilitar diagnósticos, a fim de atender às necessidades do paciente, de acordo com os conhecimentos técnicos e científicos e as normas da Instituição, sob a luz do Código de Ética. Responsabilizar -se pelo processo de coleta e busca de materiais biológicos dos pacientes, através da separação correta das amostras, bem como gerar amostra reserva de soro, com o objetivo de garantir qualidade e disponibilidade de material biológico para os exames. Realizar o manuseio e manutenção do aparelho de Gasometria, a fim de manter a acurácia no procedimento e a qualidade do material biológico para exame.
